question: Two trains A and B start with uniform speeds at the same time from points P and Q, respectively, towards each other. After crossing each other, A takes 16 hours to reach Q and B takes 4 hours to reach P. If train A is moving with a speed of 54 km/h, the speed of B (in km/h) is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] **__Shortcut Trick__**

If, A & B two trains start from P & B respectively.

Let SA & SB be their speeds and TA and TB be the time taken to reach Q and P respectively by the train A and B

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b964b86f65bcf9c3540b6d02abe05292edcdd3199d59f58ad2a718f891e325d1.png] 

{S_Aover{S_B}} = sqrt{T_Bover {T_A}}

⇒ 54/SB = √(4/16)

⇒ 54/SB = 1/2

⇒ SB = 108 kmph

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given:

A takes 16 hours to reach Q and B takes 4 hours to reach P.

Speed of A = 54 kmph

Concept used:

Time × Speed = Distance

If, A & B two trains start from P & B respectively.

Let SA & SB be their speeds.

After "T" hours they meet at point M. They continued their journey, A took X hours and B took Y hours to reach Q and P respectively.

Then, T = √{X × Y}

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/412c604e598c225e3167a258bf436dd880c3a5c52901deb91647228a676ea947.png] 

Calculation:

Let the time taken by both of the trains to meet each other be T hours and let M be the meeting point.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/fe7cedc19c8f9f3b21bfc7cca78b5261ebd4c4bdc475158b602d24c70ab894be.png] 

Hence,

T² = 16 × 4

⇒ T = 8 (taking positive value only)

Hence, the speed of B = (54 × 8) ÷ 4 = 108 kmph

**∴ The speed of B is 108 kmph.**
